d9Obligation.standing: MANDATORY, LIVE and CROSS-UNIT. Not a deferral and not an optional follow-up. Recorded here so that a later pass reading this registry alone cannot mistake the obligation for a closed item or discharge it by editing history.
d9Obligation.what: publish a successor to docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json carrying the faultCause member `host-invariant` mapped to the existing error code SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE
d9Obligation.whyItIsLive: A checker reading the inherited artifact ALONE would REFUSE a lawful host-invariant operational-failed termination, because the inherited enum does not contain the cause. That is a real interoperability consequence for any consumer that validates against the artifact rather than against this selected composition.
d9Obligation.whatIsNotOwed: Nothing in the product source. The selected composition above is complete and self-sufficient as the law the source carries: schema, workflow mapper and this registry agree, the extension is checked against the inherited contract and its declared precedence, and no choice is left to an implementer. The distinction is CURRENT SELECTED EXTENSION (done here) versus FUTURE INTEGRATION AND QUALIFICATION of the owning artifact (owed there).
d9Obligation.neverDischargedByRepinning: docs/coop/artifacts/d9-exit-contract.v1.14.json keeps its exact bytes. Editing the historical artifact to agree would destroy the evidence that this IS an extension and would make the inheritance claim unverifiable, so the mismatch is carried as a disclosed, attributed obligation instead of being reconciled away. Publishing the successor D9 artifact belongs to that unit.
d9Obligation.enforcedAt: check-integration.py holds all three halves at once: the inherited artifact still omits the cause, the selected composition carries it, and this disclosure is present.
